threads.body:
@copilot Update this PR directly for the user's revised decision: keep R2DBC Proxy 1.1.7.RELEASE and establish real R2DBC SPI 0.9 compatibility coverage alongside SPI 1.0, instead of dropping SPI 0.9 support. This supersedes the earlier request to require SPI 1.0. Do not downgrade the proxy, bundle an old second proxy, or create another PR.

Restore the supported SPI minimum to 0.9.0.RELEASE if verified. Remove this PR's SPI-1.0-only Muzzle range, the skip("0.9.0.RELEASE", "0.9.1.RELEASE") exception and its comment, and the breaking-change changelog entry for dropping 0.9. Keep assertInverse and make the supported range truthful. Preserve the existing r2dbc-1.0 module/artifact/package/scope names and normal enablement aliases; no gratuitous naming migration or runtime version gate is requested. Do not edit docs/instrumentation-list.yaml: it is generated nightly.

Add isolated, persistent test coverage for SPI 0.9 in both javaagent and standalone library integration paths while retaining SPI 1.0 coverage and existing database fixtures. The current shared testing project pulls H2 1.0.0.RELEASE, MariaDB 1.1.3 and PostgreSQL 1.0.7.RELEASE, all of which request SPI 1.0. r2dbc-proxy 1.1.7 also requests SPI 1.0. Ensure the 0.9 suite actually compiles and runs against SPI 0.9.0.RELEASE rather than being silently upgraded. An H2-only isolated suite using io.r2dbc:r2dbc-h2:0.9.0.RELEASE is a promising small approach: its POM requests SPI 0.9.0.RELEASE, it supports filter/flatMap, and it needs no Docker. Reuse repository JvmTestSuite and shared-fixture patterns; wire additional suites into check. Verify effective dependency graphs with dependencyInsight or equivalent evidence, not new module-specific runtime version-assertion infrastructure. Keep existing 1.0 behavior and coverage intact.

Cover ordinary query consumption, filtered-result consumption via flatMap, map(Function), and plain and filtered update counts with proper query-span completion. SPI 0.9 must preserve Integer counts and SPI 1.0 Long counts without conversion or ClassCastException. Include focused error/cancellation coverage where needed for the affected completion paths, reusing existing helpers. Source investigation found the SPI Result method descriptors are identical after generic erasure; RowMetadata.getColumnNames was removed in 1.0 but is not used by the proxy. Proxy 1.1.7 uses dynamic proxies and Object result forwarding; no concrete SPI 0.9 incompatibility has been identified. Its upstream compatibility table only documents SPI 1.0, so tests must establish our actual behavior rather than assume it. The current FilterAwareResult implements Publisher<Long> getRowsUpdated because the effective compile classpath was already SPI 1.0; account for that when choosing baseline compilation without unchecked element conversion or version-specific production forks unless genuinely necessary.

For the standalone library, ensure the published dependency graph can really coexist with SPI 0.9 instead of r2dbc-proxy's transitive SPI 1.0 silently upgrading consumers. Inspect how library(...) is compileOnly/test-only in repository conventions and choose the smallest correct dependency declaration/exclusion that preserves the intended SPI availability for consumers. Verify the publication metadata as well as test configurations. Preserve shading and Spring starter behavior; avoid unrelated Spring baseline changes. Update relevant handwritten supported-version usage docs only to reflect verified support, without migration history or telemetry inventories. Keep current proxy bug fixes and filtered-result completion behavior.

Run narrow formatting, targeted 0.9 and 1.0 javaagent/library tests, and relevant Muzzle checks. Report exact evidence and genuine blockers. If a substantive incompatibility appears, report the concrete failure rather than silently downgrading the proxy, skipping the failing scenario, reverting to dropping 0.9, or adding a broad workaround. Do not edit the PR title or description, reply to human reviewers, resolve threads, merge, or wait for CI. The coordinator will update PR metadata after inspecting delivery.

@copilot Update this PR directly to simplify the R2DBC compatibility tests as requested by the user. Keep proxy 1.1.7.RELEASE and real SPI 0.9 plus 1.0 coverage in both javaagent and standalone-library paths. This is a test refactor, not a return to the superseded SPI-1.0-only proposal.

Replace the separate 244-line AbstractR2dbcSpi09Test and the PR's 117-line addition of equivalent SPI 1.0 tests with one compact shared H2 result-consumption test group used by both runtime suites. Parameterize query consumption across map(BiFunction), map(Function), and filtered flatMap; parameterize update-count consumption across plain and filtered results. Keep one mapping-error and one cancellation case, shared across versions. Every case must still check its result or expected failure and query-span completion. Assert the actual update-count type and value, preserving Integer on SPI 0.9 and Long on SPI 1.0 without conversions that hide a mismatch. Share connection setup, cleanup, and span assertions instead of repeating whole methods, but avoid building a generic scenario framework or deep inheritance hierarchy merely to save lines.

Move the existing H2 filtered-result regression from AbstractR2dbcStatementTest into this shared group so coverage is not duplicated. Keep the existing multi-database tests and fixtures otherwise unchanged. Reuse the same small agent/library test setup across runtime variants where practical. Preserve isolated runtime configurations and check wiring: the 0.9 suites must not inherit the modern-driver fixture graph or the proxy's transitive SPI 1.0. Keep the standalone publication's SPI exclusion, current Muzzle range and assertInverse, production behavior, names, and current documented support unchanged. Do not edit the generated docs/instrumentation-list.yaml. The goal is materially less code and duplication without deleting the requested behavioral coverage.

Run narrow formatting and the shared H2 tests for both SPI runtimes in both instrumentation paths. Verify resolved SPI versions with dependencyInsight or equivalent output and verify the standalone generated publication metadata retains the exclusion. Keep exact command results, test counts, and dependency/publication evidence available in the coding session completion report; if execution is blocked, report the precise blocker and do not claim passing compatibility tests. Do not add committed validation-report files or runtime version-assertion infrastructure. Do not edit PR title or description, create another PR, reply to review comments, resolve threads, merge, or wait for CI. The coordinator handles metadata and reviews.
